newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market quiet, no sales - feedlot.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market quiet, no sales - feedlot.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Friday were quiet, with no bids or sales reported following this week's active trading that cleaned out most showlists, feedlot sources said.
Showlists next week were seen larger, but still containing a large number of unfinished cattle.
Cattle next week were expected to be priced at $74.00 per cwt, up $2.00 from this week's sales in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, the sources said.
Prices were seen supported by continued tight supplies of choice graded cattle and ongoing firm beef demand, they said.
Strong beef demand was tied to retail orders for features following the Thanksgiving Day holiday on November 28, market sources said.
Beef prices Thursday were quoted up $0.15 to $0.45 per cwt for choice and down $0.43 to $0.62 for selects, according to USDA. The choice heavyweight value was up $3.68 from Friday.
There were 253 fabricated loads sold Thursday, which brought the four day total to 952, up 28.1 percent from the same period a week ago at 743.
